Rose-window tracery fractured into razor-petal lobes, stone veins stained black with centuries of soot and dried rain.
Flying buttresses arcing outward like skeletal ribs, each pier capped with a leering stone face splitting at the seams.
Spire-pinnacles bristling with crockets carved as curling thorns, silhouetted jagged against a blood-bruised sky at every tower crown.
Gargoyle in full profile crouched at parapet edge, wings folded tight, jaw split wide, channeling black water from stone throat.
Grotesques lining the cornice in a leering procession, each face unique in its anguish, mouths frozen mid-scream above the nave.
Wrought-iron weathervane twisted into a rampant wyvern, oxidized to near-black, spinning loose on a corroded spire spike above.
Stone-angel statuary flanking the grand entry, faces worn smooth by acid rain, hands raised in gestures now stripped of meaning.
Dragon-head water-spouts projecting from the chapel gutters, scaled necks stretched long, open jaws pouring dark cascades into the courtyard below.
Bat-motif finials crowning every iron fence post, wings spread flat, eyes drilled hollow, repeated in regimented rows down the approach.
Vaulted arch keystone carved as a screaming visage, its open mouth the precise centerpoint where two great ribs of stone converge.
Relief-saint carvings recessed into blind niches, halos chipped to stumps, robes worn flat, identities lost beneath generations of encrusted grime.
Pointed-arch windows rising three stories, their lancet tips nearly kissing the ceiling vault above, leaded glass dark with iron-oxide staining.
Ironwork-spike rows topping every perimeter wall, each shaft hand-forged irregular, tips filed to needle points darkened by decades of weather.
Carved-rose carvings blooming in shallow relief across the tympanum, petals undercut deep enough to cast hard shadows at every hour.
Gothic tracery webbing the upper triforium, stone filaments branching and rejoining like frozen lightning preserved in cathedral-grey limestone overhead.
Decorative crenellation stepping the roofline in rhythmic notches, each merlon capped with a small carved skull worn nearly featureless by frost.
Iron-bound doors banded in wide straps stamped with rune-bands, the symbols inlaid with darker metal, handles cast as coiled serpent forms.
Oxidized-copper roof patches glowing verdigris-green against the black slate field, edges ragged where old solder joints have long since given way.
Iron-cage braziers suspended on heavy chains from the gatehouse arch, filled with smoldering pitch-soaked timber casting stuttering amber light below.
Clustered colonettes bundled tight as organ pipes rising from a single plinth, capitals carved with intertwining vine-and-bone motifs at each arch spring.
Blind arcading marching along the crypt exterior, each blind arch framing a shallow niche packed with carved foliage rotting into abstraction.
Ribbed vaulting spreading across the undercroft ceiling in dense fan-patterns, every rib edge chamfered sharp, intersections locked with grotesque carved bosses.
Tracery wheel embedded in the gable end, its spokes radiating from a central eye of hollow stone barely held by thin mullions.
Corbelled gallery projecting from the tower face, each corbel carved as a different contorted figure bearing the weight of the walkway above.
Crocket-edged gable rising steeply above the transept portal, its raking sides thick with carved leaf-forms curling outward like petrified breaking waves.
Rose-window tracery shattered into frost-fern patterns, each stone petal catching moonlight like cracked bone lacework across a cathedral's hollow eye.
Flying buttresses arching outward like skeletal ribs, their stone haunches gripping the nave wall with the desperate clutch of drowning hands.
Spire-pinnacles crowned with crockets curling like blackened thorns, each carved hook a frozen claw reaching upward through perpetual ash-colored fog.
Gargoyles locked in profile along the parapet ledge, their stone tongues extended, rain-channels carved through hollowed throats into perpetual silent screaming.
Grotesques pressed into cornice shadows, their faces half-dissolved by centuries of acid rain, mouths agape in expressions no living sculptor intended.
